senses.definition: A drawing or picture that shows something from a story or helps explain a subject.
senses.example: The illustration showed what Peter Rabbit saw in the garden.

senses.definition: Using words or word sounds in a surprising way to make an effect or a joke.
senses.example: The riddle depended on wordplay about two things called a jam.

senses.definition: A traditional story people pass from one teller to another over time.
senses.example: My aunt learned that folktale from her grandmother.

senses.definition: Stories about imagined characters or events, even when some details come from real life.
senses.example: We read a story about a talking spider in the fiction section.

senses.definition: A person who creates a piece of music.
senses.example: The composer wrote a different part for each instrument.

senses.definition: A story performed onstage mainly through singing and music.
senses.example: We could read the opera’s story before the singers came onstage.

senses.definition: Making up part of a performance as you do it.
senses.example: The trumpet player used improvisation to change the end of the tune.

senses.definition: Singing made-up sounds or syllables in place of words, often in jazz.
senses.example: The quick scat singing sounded almost like a trumpet solo.

senses.definition: A material made by weaving, knitting, or otherwise joining threads or fibers.
senses.example: The textile had a rough surface and bright blue stripes.

senses.definition: An arrangement of shapes that can cover a flat surface without gaps or overlaps.
senses.example: Rows of matching square tiles made a tessellation.

senses.definition: A closed flat shape made by joining straight sides.
senses.example: A rectangle and a triangle are both polygons.

senses.definition: One flat surface of a solid shape.
senses.example: We counted all six faces of the box.

senses.definition: A line where two faces of a solid shape meet, or the outside of a flat shape.
senses.example: I ran my finger along one edge of the cube.

senses.definition: A point where sides or edges meet, like the corner of a triangle or box.
senses.example: Each vertex of the box touches three edges.

senses.definition: A shape with two matching flat ends that are parallel, like the round ends of a can, joined by a side surface.
senses.example: The rolled-up poster formed a hollow cylinder.

senses.definition: A solid shape with a round or other closed base and sides that narrow to a single point.
senses.example: The paper party hat looked like a cone.

senses.definition: A round three-dimensional shape with every point on its surface the same distance from its center.
senses.example: The ball was almost a perfect sphere.

senses.definition: A clock that shows the time with hands that move around a face.
senses.example: The short hand of the analog clock was between three and four.

senses.definition: How much time goes by between the start and end of an activity or event.
senses.example: The elapsed time between our two stops was forty minutes.

senses.definition: A graph that shows data by placing dots over the matching marks on a number line.
senses.example: Our dot plot had two dots over nine because two leaves were that length.
